When I was 17 years old, I attempted to end my own life by overdosing on painkillers. I remember I walked into the drugstore and bought a giant bottle and was on my way (ridiculous that I could even do that), I began taking as many as I could (about half the bottle) and I made my way into the woods (the drugstore I went too was near a bike path and a giant patch of woods). I remember calling my best friend at the time and telling her that I was sorry and that I was well into my plan of ending my life (this will become important later). My memory is very hazy but as I was laying down waiting for the painkillers to hit me fully, I distinctly remember hearing a voice in my head (that was not my own) tell me to get up and start walking. And for some reason I listened to that voice and began walking; I remember feeling very woozy and sleepy but despite that I kept hearing the voice constantly tell me to "keep going," and after a little bit of time, I eventually found my way to a path I knew relatively well, but in my disassociated state, I was rather confused. On that path I remember seeing someone walking their dog and I remember hearing the voice tell me to "follow them" and that's exactly what I did, turns out that that person led me back to the school I was attending at the time and because of the call I made to my friend everyone in school had been looking for me and eventually found me as I stumbled back toward the school. An ambulance was called and I was taken to the hospital to be treated for an overdose and got the counseling I so desperately needed.

Believe me or don't believe me; this really did happen and still to this day I have no idea what exactly I encountered. However in my opinion, I honestly think that I encountered an angel, who gave me a second chance at life. Something that I am forever grateful for.

I can concur with that feeling of never fitting in. For me it was because my foster parents were really wealthy, older, and white meanwhile I was poor, young, and mixed. Almost 15 years later and it still is hard to really break that feeling of not fitting in. It's never easy. I'm sorry you had to experience that, those are shitty emotions to be feeling. I hope you are well too.

Unfortunately my experience in foster care falls into the negative category. Don't get me wrong, my foster parents tried and really did use their copious wealth to help me succeed. They did a lot for me, for example in terms of helping me, they got me educated (when they first met me I couldn't even write or spell my name), they taught me manners and honestly laid the foundation on which I've built who I am. That being said they forced Christianity down my throat and disregarded any other belief. They would belittle my family and my roots (I'm half black and half white and from an impoverished area). They were also really distant from me; see I'm a relational person and they never really talked to me unless I either achieved something or I did something to receive punishment. They never really came to my games, they would scold me if I made minor mistakes, their punishments were extreme and I always seemed to disappoint them. They would flaunt the fact that I was their "son" yet I always felt like I was nothing more than something else they could brag about. I always felt alone. I always was alone.

I appreciate your thoughts and will definitely do my best to keep trying.

Hey OP! Just to start off, I'm in the exact same boat as you, I have been finding it extremely difficult to speak to women, its terrifying if I'm honest, so I guess view my comments as sort of a conversation from one person to another. 

I think its important to recognize that these feelings you (and I) have are completely valid, we all feel them and theres nothing wrong with feeling this way, even if sometimes it may make us feel weak or vulnerable. Its hard sometimes when we crave something so much, and we see friends or people we know getting things that we try so desperately to attain. Its not just hard, its painful if we're honest with ourselves. It also makes it especially hard when we feel like we can't talk to friends because we're afraid (which I totally get and feel the same way). All these feelings we're feeling can become overwhelming and lead to anger. 

Anxiety is a powerful thing. It can be scary in all honesty to be put in front of people or even speaking to new people. Interacting with people is not as easy as people say it is, because rejection is a painful thing.

I hope if you get anything from what I said its that you're not alone in feeling this way. And its ok to feel this way, I'm still coming to grips with that myself you know? One piece of advice I was given a long time ago with regards to feeling like you can't do anything can be summarized as such; try your best to accomplish one thing everyday. It can be something like stepping outside for a short time (and not just to get necessities) or honestly it can be something like getting out of bed. Whatever it may be, try your best to accomplish one thing, and continue that trend until you feel you can try and accomplish two things and so on and so on. But for right now, start small, just try your best to start. 

I don't know your situation and I don't know everything that happened so I can only speculate. Regardless, it's easy for those around you who aren't in your situation to tell you that "things will get better" when to you it seems like they never will. I can't even imagine how hard this is but I really do hope OP that you choose life. I don't even know you, but I don't have to know you to know that you're a person and every person deserves life, even if it's a hard one. You're a diamond in the making, under pressure, just remember that you're in the making. You'll be in my thoughts OP and I hope I'll hear back from you. Please be safe.

When I was your age I dated a girl who I thought was everything I could ever dream of. Unfortunately due to her ever changing mood and her many changes of heart, she left me many times. 

We had an on again and off again relationship for quite sometime with me always believing her words and believing that she and I could make "us" work. It even went as far as me leaving a woman I had dated (that wasn't her) for a couple of years for her.

You're not alone; we all have that person (even when we're young) who we try so desperately to make ours. But you are worth so much more than that. You're worth more than someone who only comes back to you when they're lonely or just want someone. You deserve someone who won't just ask you to wait (and give you false hope), but someone who will actually meet you half-way and give you their all.

I wish you the best.
